chunks: From him, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahbub, from Khalil ibn Amr al-Yashkuri, from Jamil ibn Darradj, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) used to say: 'When the boy is moderate in semen production, small in size, and calm in gaze, he is among those from whom good is hoped and evil is feared [i.e., safe from]. And he said: 'When the boy is intense in semen production, large in size, sharp in gaze, he is among those from whom good is not hoped and evil is not feared [i.e., not safe from].'

key_terms.يُؤْمَنُ شَرُّهُ: His evil is feared/safe from (i.e., he is safe from mischief)

ai.seo_question: What are the physical signs that determine if a young boy is considered mature enough for marriage in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: Attributed to Imam al-Sadiq (AS) and citing Imam Ali (AS), this hadith establishes the criteria for distinguishing between a minor and a mature boy based on physical development and temperament, which is crucial for determining the validity of their consent in marriage contracts. The contrast between the 'moderate' boy, whose goodness is hoped for and evil feared, and the 'intense' boy, who is neither, highlights the Shia juristic emphasis on behavioral maturity as a marker of legal capacity (bulugh).
